svg.title: How one Grok Bot task moves forward
svg.desc: A goal and a stop line reach the shared computer. Plugins come first; otherwise the task uses that Bot's screen. Sensitive input returns to the user, and risky actions go through Auto Review. HTTP 200 only starts a run.
svg.text: One task: from a sentence to a checkable result
Example: draft five follow-ups in this chat and wait. Do not send email or change the CRM.
1 Goal and stop line in the same message
Name the artifact, where it lands, and what must not happen
2 Work on the shared cloud computer
Use a plugin when one exists. Otherwise use this Bot's screen
One computer-use task per Bot; other Bots can still run in parallel
3 Hand sensitive input back
Password, two-factor, CAPTCHA, payment
A masked secret stays out of the transcript. Do not paste it into chat
4 Risky actions go through Auto Review
A separate review model: allow, ask, or deny
Approval covers this proposal. It does not undo work already done
5 Read the result back in the chat
Done, waiting, or failed. Closing the laptop does not stop the cloud turn
6 Automate only after the path is stable
A skill records how. A routine records when, and runs with the laptop closed
Webhook HTTP 200: accepted and started, not finished
A teaching order, not six required services on every task.
Hiding a Bot does not pause its routines. Deleting a Bot removes them, not the shared files and sign-ins.
Learning schematic. The computer-use stack is unpublished.
Sources: public Cursor / xAI docs and the Routines help page · 2026-09-28
